# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫰 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

My thinking: Let me trace who can reach whom. Mute can hear but cannot speak, so Mute's only output is gestures. Blind can speak but cannot see, so Blind reaches Mute directly by voice, but Mute can only answer Blind through me. I can speak (both hear me) and gesture (only Mute sees), and I never hear anyone — so replies to me must come as gestures, which I can see.

This round Mute sent me seven gestures: 👋 🫰 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🫴. My best reading is a greeting, a reference to the manual (writing hand), and one-two-three pointing — likely Mute identifying the three wires and asking what I see. Blind waved 👋, probably just announcing presence.

The most urgent thing is to get my full visual report into the ears of both of them at once, since I can speak to everyone, and to establish a small fixed code so Mute can answer me in gestures and I can relay aloud for Blind. I'll propose: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ☝✌🤟 = wires 1/2/3, ✍ = "the manual", 🫴 = "question". I'll also acknowledge Mute's message with a thumbs-up so they know I received it and am answering by voice.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf speaking, so you both hear me. I can see the bomb, I can never hear anyone, and I cannot touch it. Since I speak last each round, you get this at the start of the next one. Full view of the bomb: display reads zero. One indicator light, and it is blue. One large button printed with the words: push to defuse. Three wires: wire one blue, wire two green, wire three yellow, and I read them as numbered left to right. Nothing else is printed on it. Mute, I saw your seven gestures. I guess the pointing hands meant wire one, wire two, wire three, and the writing hand meant the manual. From now on answer me like this: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, one, two, three fingers mean wire one, two, three, the writing hand means the manual, open palm up means you are asking me a question. Whatever you sign to me, I will say out loud so Blind hears it too. Blind, I saw your wave. You can speak to Mute directly and Mute will hear you, but Mute cannot answer you except through me, and I cannot hear you, so if you ever need to tell me something, gesture it and I will see it. Mute, please look up whatever the manual says about a zero display, a blue light, a large push-to-defuse button, and three wires that are blue, green, yellow in that order, and confirm or correct my reading of your gestures.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

Helpfully the mapping is symmetric, so whichever direction it reads, the order comes out the same: yellow (3) first, green (2) second, blue (1) last. But this is not confirmed, and a wrong cut kills everyone — so Blind must not touch anything until Mute explicitly confirms and I call a go. Blind's 👍✍ is just an acknowledgement; Blind only knows the manual exists through my speech. My speech is the only bridge carrying Mute's knowledge to Blind's hands, so this turn I relay my full interpretation aloud, ask Mute targeted yes/no confirmations plus the meaning of the ambiguous signs (🤌, ✊, 🫰) and what the manual says about the zero display and blue light, and I echo the number pairs back in gestures as a checkable question.

speak(text="This is Deaf. Mute, here is what I think your signs said. Everyone note: this is not yet confirmed, so nobody acts on it. Your second message was the manual sign, then thumbs down, then a fist. I read that as: the manual says do not press the button. Your next three messages were the manual sign, then a snap sign, then number pairs: one then three, two then two, three then one, with pinched fingers between the numbers. I read that as a cutting order: wire one is cut third, wire two is cut second, wire three is cut first. That means, if I am right: cut the yellow wire, wire three, first; then the green wire, wire two; then the blue wire, wire one, last. I am signing those same three number pairs back to you right now, ending with the open palm as my question mark. Mute: gesture thumbs up if that reading is correct, thumbs down if it is wrong. Also answer these: does the pinched fingers sign mean cut? Does the fist mean press the button, or does it mean stop and wait? And what does the snap sign before each pair mean? Blind, you heard all of that. Do not cut anything and do not press anything yet. Wait for my explicit go, which I will only give after Mute confirms. Blind, please speak now: tell us everything you can feel under your hands. How many wires, how they are positioned, whether the button moves or resists, any bumps, ridges or labels you can feel, anything Mute's manual might need to match against.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤌", "🤟", "✌", "🤌", "✌", "🤟", "🤌", "☝", "🫴"])

Question one: did your thumbs-down mean that my stated order, cut wire three first, then wire two, then wire one, was wrong? Question eight: does the correct solution involve pressing the button at all? Question nine: does the manual need any fact about this bomb that I have not already told you? Question ten: is the complete instruction for Blind exactly this: cut wire three, then wire two, then wire one, and never press the button? This round, speak to Mute and describe everything your hands tell you: how many wires and how they run, whether the wires differ in thickness or texture, any ridges, bumps or braille near them, which end you count as wire one, whether the button depresses and how it resists, and any other parts you can find.
